title: Nimbus POC scoping - open models
summary: POC scoping to select open-model shortlist for a 2-week pilot focused on multilingual analytics extraction. Discussed success criteria (accuracy > 88% on key intents, latency <200ms p50), workload sizing (~500k tokens/day), benchmarks to run, and timeline for delivery. Next steps: Redwood to run latency/quality benchmarks on 3 models and share bench spreadsheet + security docs, Nimbus to provide 200 labelled samples and priority intents.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark spreadsheet + security pack by 2026-05-14
Mateo: run latency + quality runs (Llama-3 13B, Mistral 7B, Falcon 40B) by 2026-05-19
Nimbus: share 200 labelled multilingual samples and priority intents by 2026-05-15
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting w/ infra by 2026-05-21
action_items: Mateo Ruiz: run 3-model latency & QA benchmark (Llama-3 13B, Mistral 7B, Falcon 40B) - due 2026-05-19
Jenna Park: send security docs (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS details) and pricing template - due 2026-05-14
Priya Shah: provide 200 labelled samples + success metric spreadsheet - due 2026-05-15
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jenna Park, Mateo Ruiz (Redwood); Priya Shah, Daniel Kim, Sara O'Neill (Nimbus)

[00:00] Jenna (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro, i'm jenna park, our ae, and with me is mateo, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya (Nimbus): thanks jenna, i'm priya, head of ml at nimbus, we run a document extraction/policy analytics product, mostly multi-lingual (en/es/fr, some pt).
[00:28] Mateo (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda — define success criteria for the poc, sizing/throughput, shortlist open models, runbench plan, timeline. sound ok?
[00:40] Daniel (Nimbus Infra): yep, and i want to make sure the VPC setup and data retention questions are covered.
[00:47] Jenna: absolutely, we'll cover private deployment concerns and what we need from infra.
[00:52] Priya: high level — our goal is to evaluate open-models for extraction quality on domain docs (contracts, policies) + latency/cost in our infra. success criteria we care about are: accuracy on key intents > 88%, false positive rate under 5% for named entities, and inference latency p50 under 200ms on our planned footprint.
[01:10] Mateo: ok noted. what's your expected qps / tokens per day?
[01:14] Sara (Product): current peak is about 12 qps, avg payload ~180 tokens, daily active about 3k users -> rough estimate ~500k tokens/day. we'll design for headroom x2.
[01:25] Mateo: good, that helps sizing. for the open-model shortlist we propose starting with Llama-3 13B (llama3), Mistral 7B v1, and Falcon 40B opt-quantized variant as a heavier baseline. tradeoffs: Llama-3 tends to be strong on instruction tuning and multilingual, Mistral is very cost-efficient for many tasks, Falcon 40B can hit quality for complex reasoning but heavier.
[01:50] Priya: curious about Mistral's multilingual performance — we've seen mixed results in spanish.
[01:56] Mateo: yeah, Mistral 7B is ok on spanish but might lag for domain-specific legal phrasing. Llama-3 13B has better multilingual alignment but at higher cost. also quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) change performance and latency; we should bench both accuracy and token throughput.
[02:14] Daniel: what's the recommended infra for the pilot? we have GCP with T4s and some A10s available.
[02:20] Mateo: for 13B, an A10 or A100 gives best p50 latency; T4 is ok for throughput but p99 can jump. for Mistral 7B, T4s are often fine. Falcon 40B we'll need A100-class for reasonable latency. we can simulate on our dedicated infra and provide expected numbers.
[02:41] Jenna: important to highlight caching — prefix/KV cache helps reduce cost for repeated flows, but for extraction across different docs it's less effective. we'll still include caching config in the bench.
[02:55] Priya: success criteria — besides the accuracy thresholds we mentioned, we want to measure hallucination rate on entity extraction and stability across languages. also cost per 10k tokens target to compare to our current baseline (we pay X with another vendor).
[03:12] Mateo: got it — we'll report p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 10k tokens (est), and quality metrics (precision/recall/F1 on supplied labels).
[03:22] Sara: timeline — how long to run the bench and get results?
[03:26] Mateo: bench runs typically take 3-4 business days once we have the labelled sample set and infra access. then we'll do a short QA pass, total 5 business days to share a runnable report. if we parallelize models we can do in 3 days.
[03:40] Jenna: so proposed pilot timeline: week 1 (2026-05-18) kickoff, Redwood runs bench and shares results by 2026-05-21, week 2 pilot tuning and small integration tests, pilot review by 2026-05-26. does that align with your timeline?
[03:55] Priya: yes that works. we'll aim to get the 200 labelled multilingual samples over to you by 2026-05-15.
[04:02] Daniel: we need to understand networking — can Redwood run experiments against our VPC endpoint or do you need sample data only?
[04:09] Mateo: we can do either. easiest is to have you upload anonymized samples to a secure bucket we can pull from; alternatively we can deploy a private Redwood agent in your VPC for on-prem style testing. we'll include both options in the security pack.
[04:23] Priya: encryption and KMS is a must — we cannot have keys managed externally.
[04:27] Jenna: noted. we'll include KMS/HSM options and SOC2/ISO summaries.
[04:31] Priya: what about model fallback / graceful degradation? if latency spikes, we'd like an automatic fallback to a smaller model to preserve UX.
[04:38] Mateo: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback — you can set policies by latency or cost. we'll prototype a fallback policy in the pilot: default route to Llama3 13B, fallback to Mistral 7B when p95 > 500ms.
[04:52] Sara: any thoughts on quantization vs fp16 quality tradeoff?
[04:56] Mateo: quantization (4-bit) reduces memory and increases throughput but sometimes reduces precision on entity extraction; we'll test 8-bit and 4-bit quantized checkpoints for each model and report delta in F1.
[05:08] Priya: do you have existing benchmarks on hallucination rates for these models?
[05:12] Jenna: we have internal benches but they're workload-dependent; we'll run the bench on your supplied labels so it's apples-to-apples.
[05:18] Daniel: security question — audit logs and RBAC, we require per-user traceability.
[05:22] Mateo: Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdown and audit logs; RBAC via SSO/SAML is supported. we'll include screenshots in the pack.
[05:34] Priya: ok, pricing — rough estimate for pilot?
[05:38] Jenna: for a 2-week pilot at ~500k tokens/day with three models tested, rough hosted estimate is low thousands, but we'll provide exact pricing options: hosted trial credits vs dedicated reserved capacity estimates.
[05:50] Sara: competitors — we are also evaluating OpenAI and Anthropic for quality and Bedrock for infra fit.
[05:56] Mateo: understood, we'll make sure the bench shows latency/cost tradeoffs so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[06:03] Priya: any blockers we should know?
[06:05] Jenna: main blockers: getting labelled samples, infra access decision (bucket vs VPC agent), and agreeing on success metrics.
[06:14] Priya: we'll prioritize samples and finalize infra with daniel.
[06:18] Jenna: recap and next steps — Jenna to send security pack + pricing spreadsheet; Mateo to run benchmarks on Llama-3 13B, Mistral 7B, Falcon 40B (including quantized variants) and share results; Nimbus to provide 200 labelled multilingual samples and confirm infra approach.
[06:36] Daniel: ok thanks all, schedule kickoff once jenna sends docs.
[06:39] Jenna: thanks everyone, end call.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), occasional speaker attribution artifacts. Links shared: benchmark-template.xlsx (drive link), redwood-security-pack.pdf (drive link).
